around.headline: Bengaluru nurse chased, attacked with machete; acid thrown by husband in J.P. Nagar
around.summary: A nurse in J.P. Nagar was chased and attacked with a machete by her husband, who also threw acid at her, per The Times of India and NDTV. If you or someone you know is facing escalating threats from a partner, involve the police (100) or a domestic-violence helpline before it turns violent — don't wait for one dramatic incident to act.

around.headline: 18-year-old dies of electrocution during Ganesha immersion in Karnataka
around.summary: An 18-year-old died of electrocution during a Ganesha idol immersion in Karnataka, likely from stray current spreading through water near temporary electrical setups, per The Times of India. Avoid entering water near lights, cables or speakers at immersion sites, even if others are already in it.

around.headline: Traffic curbs for Ganesha immersion processions across Bengaluru on September 18
around.summary: Bengaluru traffic police have announced diversions and restrictions for immersion processions tomorrow, September 18, per Deccan Herald and The New Indian Express. If your commute passes near lake routes or procession paths, plan for delays or an alternate route.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The New Indian Express

around.headline: Karnataka High Court flags illegal PG operations in Bengaluru, orders safety guidelines
around.summary: The Karnataka High Court has flagged large-scale illegal paying-guest (PG) operations in the city and issued sweeping safety guidelines, per Live Law. If you live in a PG, it's worth checking that your building has basic fire-safety measures like clear exits and extinguishers.

around.headline: GBA orders removal of 'overnight temple' at South Bengaluru apartment complex
around.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has ordered removal of an unauthorised 'overnight temple' structure that came up at a South Bengaluru apartment complex, per The Hindu. Residents dealing with similar unauthorised structures in their complex can flag it to GBA/BBMP for action.

around.headline: Centre's plan to charge for instant UPI payments draws flak from Bengaluru businesses
around.summary: A proposal to levy a fee on instant UPI payments has drawn criticism from Bengaluru traders and is being debated nationally, per Al Jazeera and The Times of India. If you run a small business or pay via UPI often, watch for updates before any charge takes effect.
around.source: Al Jazeera, The Times of India

around.headline: India warns new US tariffs over Russian oil purchases could hurt ties
around.summary: India has warned that fresh US tariffs tied to its continued purchase of Russian oil could strain bilateral ties, per Al Jazeera. Prolonged trade friction could eventually feed through to fuel and import costs, so it's worth watching how talks develop.

street_smart.title: You're helping carry a Ganesha idol into a lake for immersion this evening. Strings of decorative lights and loudspeaker cables run along the bank, and some cables are lying in puddles right where people are wading in — like the immersion site where an 18-year-old died of electrocution in Karnataka today. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: an 18-year-old died of electrocution during a Ganesha immersion in Karnataka, likely from stray current spreading through water near temporary electrical setups (The Times of India). Electrical safety at immersion/public events hasn't been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: Hundreds of people are already wading through the same water, and the event feels routine — but the cables and puddles near the bank haven't been checked by anyone official.

choices.text: Wade in with everyone else — if the setup were dangerous, the organizers or the crowd wouldn't be doing it.
choices.feedback: Risky. A crowd doing something isn't proof it's safe — mass immersion events are exactly where stray-current incidents happen, precisely because everyone assumes someone else has already checked.

choices.text: Avoid the puddles and any cables, railings or poles near the water; point out the loose wiring to the organizers or call BESCOM's complaint line so it gets fixed before more people wade in.
choices.feedback: Correct. Stray current in water doesn't announce itself, so the safest move is to stay out of any puddle near electrical equipment and get it flagged to someone who can cut power or reroute the cabling.

choices.text: Walk through the puddle instead of stepping directly on a cable — you're not touching the wire, so it should be fine.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. If a live wire is touching wet ground, current spreads through the whole puddle, not just the point of contact — you don't need to touch the wire itself to be electrocuted, only stand in the same water. This is very likely what happened in today's fatal incident.

choices.text: Take a video of the hazard to post online later so authorities take notice.
choices.feedback: Risky. Documenting a hazard is useful afterward, but it does nothing about the danger in front of you right now — and anyone else nearby is still at risk until it's physically flagged or fixed on the spot.

takeaways: Water conducts electricity: a live wire touching wet ground can electrify an entire puddle, not just the exact spot it touches — treat any puddle near temporary lighting or speaker cables at an event as unsafe.
If you spot exposed or submerged wiring at a public event, tell the organizers immediately or call BESCOM's complaint number (1912) rather than assuming someone has already checked.
If someone is down and may still be in contact with electricity, don't touch them directly — cut the power at the source or use a dry wooden stick/rod to separate them, then call 108.

quiz.question: What did the Karnataka High Court recently flag in Bengaluru, ordering sweeping safety guidelines?
quiz.why: Many PGs operate without basic fire-safety measures like clear exits or extinguishers — worth checking if you live in one.

quiz.question: A Centre proposal to charge a fee on instant UPI payments has drawn criticism from which group in Bengaluru?
quiz.why: UPI merchant payments have largely been fee-free since a 2020 zero-MDR policy — any new charge proposal reopens that debate.

quiz.question: What caused the death of an 18-year-old during a Ganesha immersion in Karnataka this week?
quiz.why: Stray electrical current can spread through water from a single faulty wire, endangering anyone standing in the same puddle.

quiz.question: Which of these lakes is NOT located in Bengaluru?
quiz.why: Dal Lake is in Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir — Bengaluru's lakes are mostly human-made tanks built centuries ago for irrigation and drinking water.

quiz.question: If someone may still be in contact with a live electrical wire, what should you do first before helping them?
options: Pull them away with your bare hands
Cut the power source or use a dry wooden stick to separate them
Pour water on them to cool the current
Shout at them to let go
quiz.why: Touching a person still in contact with live current can electrocute you too — always cut the power or use a non-conductive object first, then call 108.
